name: Rolen Depot Utility Trouser
description: Simple, no-frills work trousers in dark brown or black, sold by the pallet-load to Tier 1 and Tier 2 employers for issue to shift workers. Straight cut, flat front, two side pockets and two back pockets. The fabric is coarse and stiff when new and takes months of washing to soften. Ubiquitous on the Shelf.
what_it_says: You're drawing a shift wage somewhere, or you bought the cheapest thing available and it happened to be this.
story_hooks: Rolen Depot trousers are sold in bulk by gray-market resellers — a batch with an unusual dye lot might trace back to a corporate stockroom theft.
Because they're so generic, they're sometimes deliberately chosen by people who want to disappear into a crowd on the Shelf.

physical_description.visual_profile: Utilitarian silhouette with zero aesthetic pretension—a straight, unflinching column of fabric from hip to ankle. The cut suggests function over form: practical, forgettable, deliberately generic. On-body, they read as pure work uniform: the visual signature of shift labor in the GLMZ.
physical_description.fit: Straight leg, relaxed through the thigh with no taper. Flat front waistband sits at natural waist. Intentionally designed to accommodate layering underneath and repetitive movement. Zero vanity in the drape.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy-duty synthetic blend—likely polyester-viscose composite with reinforced stress weave. Deliberately rough and industrial, not meant to be soft.
physical_description.texture: Coarse and stiff when new, with a dense weave that catches light flatly. Over months of wash cycles, develops a subtle sheen and slight softening at stress points (inner thighs, seat). Shows creasing readily. Fabric has a slightly waxy feel due to finish treatment.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal black or muted dark brown—colors selected for hiding grease, mineral dust, and chemical stains. No pattern. No accent colors.
physical_description.closures: Simple metal zipper fly (likely stamped steel, industrial grade). Single button at waistband. No flourish.
distinctive_features: Two deep side pockets sized for gloves or small tools
Two back patch pockets, often stiffened to hold shape
No rivets, no reinforced bartacks—bottom-line manufacturing
Subtle product tag on interior waistband: 'ROLEN BASIC GOODS — ISSUED PROPERTY'
Minimal hemming; many arrive with raw or roughly finished hems meant for on-site tailoring
Takes months to break in; new pairs have an almost cardboard-like rigidity
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 issued wear. A uniform of precarity and labor. Signals employment in shift-based, low-autonomy work—warehouse, manufacturing, sanitation, logistics.
physical_description.cultural_context: The wearer is functionally invisible in the GLMZ social hierarchy. These trousers announce: I work for someone else's profit, I am issued, I am replaceable. Worn by warehouse crew, factory floor staff, Behemoth facility attendants, loading dock workers, and municipal maintenance teams. The uniform of the managed.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when issued (stiff, creased from storage). After 2-3 weeks: broken in at knees and seat, minor staining. After 6 months: softened, faded, small tears at cuffs from footwear friction, minor patching at seams. Worn until they're genuinely unwearable, then replaced by identical pair.
